answer: A farm that wants 180 keys as a result forfeits 180 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the comet seed, the quill timing is verifiable from the pearl record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 505 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
